name: Pharmacy Technology
description: Receiving and verifying prescriptions, entering them, compounding and prepacking preparations, and maintaining drug storage and security — under a pharmacist's supervision, in a retail pharmacy, a hospital or a compounding facility. ⚠⚠ Unlike most short allied-health certificates, this one is REGULATED: section 465.014, F.S. requires anyone who wishes to work as a pharmacy technician in Florida to register with the Board of Pharmacy and to have completed a board-approved training programme. Taught at 30 Florida public institutions.
degreesNote: ⚠⚠ THE BOARD-APPROVED PROGRAMME IS THE WHOLE POINT, so check the approval before you pay. Section 465.014 requires registration with the Florida Board of Pharmacy, and the application asks for completion of a training programme the board has approved. A programme the board has not approved does not get you registered, and without registration you cannot work. ⚠ The statute also limits how many technicians a pharmacist may supervise — one, unless the board's guidelines permit more — which is a real constraint on how many jobs exist per pharmacy counter. Florida's programme is a single block: PTN0084, PTN0085 and PTN0086, Pharmacy Technician 1, 2 and 3, at 360, 300 and 300 clock hours, carried by 21 institutions each. ⚠⚠⚠ Note what is NOT there: unlike medical assisting, there are no occupational completion points and no intermediate job title. You finish all 960 hours or you have nothing to show an employer. Plan for the whole thing. ⚠ 222 of the 225 Florida credentials awarded in 2023 were one-to-two-year certificates; three were associate degrees. A handful of institutions also run it as an Applied Technology Diploma, which is college credit rather than clock hours — worth asking about if a degree might follow.

cips.note: Pharmacy Technician/Assistant — 30 Florida public institutions and 225 credentials in 2023, 222 of them one-to-two-year certificates. Carriers are predominantly district technical colleges, with a few state colleges running the college-credit Applied Technology Diploma version.

related.note: ⚠⚠ The comparison every student choosing between short allied-health certificates should make. Same pay to within $60 a year, similar length, often the same campus — but medical assisting is unregulated in Florida and has four labelled exit points you can stop and work at, while pharmacy technology is state-registered and has none. ⚠ Choose on which work you want to do, not on pay, because the pay is the same.

⚠ Named because the two get confused and they are not alike. Both involve precise handling of samples and reagents under regulation, but laboratory science is a diagnostic discipline with a long credential ladder to MLT and then MLS, while pharmacy technology tops out at the technician registration unless you go on to the pharmacy doctorate. If you want a ladder, the laboratory has one.

⚠ Not a route — separate credential, and clock hours do not transfer. Named because pharmacology is the one thing the two share, and technicians who discover they want the clinical side rather than the dispensing side routinely move across. Ask the nursing programme what, if anything, it will articulate before assuming any of it counts.
